Let \(Z_t=r_t(\cos\theta_t,\sin\theta_t)\), with \(r_t=\|Z_t\|>0\). Since the SDE is Stratonovich, ordinary calculus applies.

For \(u=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\),

\[
u^\top A u
=
u^\top(-I+aS+J)u
=
-1+a\sin 2\theta,
\]

because \(J\) is skew-symmetric. Also the noise \(bJZ_t\circ dW_t\) only rotates \(Z_t\), so it does not directly change \(r_t\). Thus

\[
d\log r_t=(-1+a\sin 2\theta_t)\,dt.
\]

The angular equation is

\[
d\theta_t=(1+a\cos 2\theta_t)\,dt+b\,dW_t.
\]

Set \(x_t=2\theta_t\pmod {2\pi}\). Then

\[
dx_t=2(1+a\cos x_t)\,dt+2b\,dW_t.
\]

This diffusion on the circle has a unique invariant density. Writing \(B=b^2\), its unnormalized density is

\[
p(x)=\int_0^{2\pi}
\exp\!\left(-\frac{s+a(\sin(x+s)-\sin x)}{B}\right)\,ds.
\]

Therefore the top Lyapunov exponent is

\[
\lambda(a,b)
=
-1+aM(a,b),
\]

where

\[
M(a,b)
=
\frac{
\displaystyle \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-s/b^2}\sin\frac{s}{2}\,
I_1\!\left(\frac{2a}{b^2}\sin\frac{s}{2}\right)\,ds
}{
\displaystyle \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-s/b^2}
I_0\!\left(\frac{2a}{b^2}\sin\frac{s}{2}\right)\,ds
},
\]

and \(I_0,I_1\) are the modified Bessel functions. This formula comes from integrating over \(x\) using

\[
\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-k\cos x}\,dx=2\pi I_0(k),
\qquad
\int_0^{2\pi}\cos x\,e^{-k\cos x}\,dx=-2\pi I_1(k).
\]

The deterministic system has eigenvalues

\[
-1\pm \sqrt{a^2-1}
\]

when \(a\ge 1\), and complex eigenvalues with real part \(-1\) when \(a<1\). Hence it is not exponentially stable exactly when

\[
a\ge \sqrt2.
\]

The stochastic origin is almost surely exponentially stable exactly when \(\lambda(a,b)<0\), i.e. \(aM(a,b)<1\).

Thus the requested set is

\[
\boxed{
\left\{(a,b):\ a\ge \sqrt2,\ b>0,\ 
a\,
\frac{
\displaystyle \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-s/b^2}\sin\frac{s}{2}\,
I_1\!\left(\frac{2a}{b^2}\sin\frac{s}{2}\right)\,ds
}{
\displaystyle \int_0^{2\pi} e^{-s/b^2}
I_0\!\left(\frac{2a}{b^2}\sin\frac{s}{2}\right)\,ds
}
<1
\right\}.
}
\]

For every such pair, one may take

\[
\gamma=1-aM(a,b)>0.
\]
